project.name: GGClips
project.summary: A proposed mobile-first clip site for adult GTA 6 fans, starting with a small group of authorized streamer partners. AI helps prepare clips, but a human checks rights and quality before anything is published.

edges.label: authorized source queued
edges.description: Registering an approved partner source starts preparation work; the resulting clip stays a draft until an editor approves it.

edges.label: editor review actions
edges.description: Editors use protected site routes to approve, reject, or suspend content.

flows.title: Find and watch a clip
flows.description: A visitor sees the age notice, finds an approved clip, and watches it with captions.

steps.note: The visitor opens the clip feed and acknowledges the adult-content notice.
The site asks for clips that are approved and publicly available.
Only published catalogue entries are returned.
The video service delivers the clip at a suitable size for the device.
The player shows controls, captions, streamer credit, and a report link.

flows.title: Prepare an authorized clip
flows.description: A partner source becomes a draft, is checked by a person, and is published only after approval.

steps.note: An editor registers a partner source and its permission evidence.
The protected route records the source and queues a preparation job.
The source file remains in private storage.
The worker transcribes, suggests moments, and prepares a review draft.
The model proposes possible moments; it does not decide rights or publish.
A draft rendition is prepared for the editor to inspect.
An editor checks context, rights, captions, framing, and content before approval.

flows.title: Report and remove a clip
flows.description: A visitor reports a concern and an editor can suspend the clip while reviewing it.

steps.note: The visitor opens the report form from a clip.
The site records the report and applies spam protections.
The report and moderation history are stored for review.
An editor reviews the case and records the decision.
The takedown action removes the clip from public listing and playback.
